dedupe_keys.name: smadi global soil moisture agricultural drought index 0 05 degree fortnightly 2010 2015

description: SMADI is a global agricultural drought index computed every two weeks from June 2010 to December 2015 on the 0.05 degree Climate Modeling Grid. The Zenodo record says it combines MODIS NDVI and land surface temperature with SMOS BEC L3 soil moisture, and uses MODIS IGBP land cover to keep only grassland and cropland mosaic pixels, with each file a 3600 by 7200 matrix in WGS84 and NaN where no retrieval was possible. It was published in June 2019 (version 1.0.0) by researchers at the University of Salamanca and the University of Valencia, supported by Spanish ministry projects, under the CC BY 4.0 licence, free to download as 146 MATLAB files of about 1.3 GB with a readme. Coverage is global agricultural land. Caveats: MATLAB format only, the series stops in 2015, and non-agricultural pixels are excluded. For simulation it gives fortnightly satellite drought hazard maps to calibrate crop loss and food supply disruption models. Related catalogue records include the DEDI global daily drought index and the EDO Combined Drought Indicator.
